questions.q: Why doesn't a container get GPU access by default, even on a machine that has a GPU?
options: A container's isolation hides host hardware like the GPU by default; it needs an explicit path to the driver
GPUs cannot be used by any containerized process
Only Windows containers support GPU access
Docker Desktop disables GPU access permanently
questions.explain: The same isolation that makes containers lightweight also hides host hardware like a GPU unless something explicitly passes it through.

questions.q: What does the NVIDIA Container Toolkit actually do?
options: It replaces Docker as the container runtime
It installs CUDA inside every image automatically
It teaches the container runtime how to pass specific host GPU devices through to a container that requests them
It compiles PyTorch from source
questions.explain: It's a plugin for the container runtime, not a replacement for it — its job is enabling GPU passthrough.

questions.q: Why does the example Dockerfile use `nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-runtime-ubuntu22.04` instead of `python:3.12-slim`?
options: It's required for any image larger than 1GB
It includes the CUDA runtime libraries a GPU-built framework like torch needs to actually run on the GPU
It makes the build faster regardless of GPU use
python:3.12-slim cannot run Python code
questions.explain: A CUDA-matched base image provides the runtime libraries a GPU build of a framework was compiled against — a mismatch here is a common source of GPU failures.

questions.q: What happens if you run a GPU-built container without the `--gpus` flag?
options: The container refuses to start
Docker automatically adds the flag for you
The build fails immediately
The container starts fine, but can't see any GPU and typically falls back to CPU silently
questions.explain: Without --gpus, there's no GPU passthrough — the container runs, but the framework inside it has no GPU to use.

questions.q: Why run `nvidia-smi` inside the container, rather than just trusting that `--gpus all` worked?
options: nvidia-smi is required to build the image
It's the only way to install CUDA
Running it inside the container is proof the GPU passthrough actually worked, not just that the flag was accepted
It has no real purpose beyond habit
questions.explain: nvidia-smi run from inside the container confirms the GPU is genuinely visible there, which is a stronger check than assuming the flag succeeded.
